Answer (A) is incorrect. A report should be made to ATC whether or not in radar contact any time you encounter any type of weather conditions that have not been forecast. If IMC were forecast, no report is necessary. Answer (C) is incorrect. A report should be made to ATC when correcting an ETA any time a previous ETA is in error in excess of 2 min., not 4 min.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: When ATC has not imposed any climb or descent restrictions and aircraft are within 1,000 feet of assigned altitude, pilots should attempt to both climb and descend at a rate of between

choices.text: 500 feet per minute and 1,000 feet per minute.
500 feet per minute and 1,500 feet per minute.
1,000 feet per minute and 2,000 feet per minute.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (AIM Para 4-4-10)
ATC 허가가 특정 고도에 내려오거나 올라갈 때, 조종사는 항공기의 운영 특성에 맞는 최적의 속도를 1,000 ft 이상 또는 그보다 낮은 고도에 사용해야 하며, 그 다음, 주어진 고도에 도달할 때까지 500~1,500 fpm 사이의 속도로 내려오거나 올라가는 시도를 해야 합니다.
또한, 항로에서는 중간 레벨 오프가 없는 항로의 중앙선에 올라 내려가야 한다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
고도의 1,000 ft. 이내에, 조종사는 1,000 fpm가 아닌 500에서 1,500 fpm 사이의 속도로 오르고/오르는 것을 시도해야 합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
고도의 1,000 ft. 이내에, 조종사는 1,000에서 2,000 fpm 사이의 속도로 오르고/오르는 것을 시도해야 합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (AIM Para 4-4-10) DISCUSSION: When ATC clearances are given to descend or climb to a certain altitude, the pilot should use the optimum rate consistent with the operating characteristics of the aircraft to 1,000 ft. above or below the assigned altitude and then attempt to descend or climb at a rate of between 500 and 1,500 fpm until reaching the assigned altitude. Also, on airways, one should climb and descend on the centerline of the airway with no intermediate level-offs. Answer (A) is incorrect. Within 1,000 ft. of the assigned altitude, pilots should attempt to climb/descend at a rate of between 500 and 1,500 fpm, not 1,000 fpm. Answer (C) is incorrect. Within 1,000 ft. of the assigned altitude, pilots should attempt to climb/descend at a rate of between 500 and 1,500 fpm, not 1,000 and 2,000 fpm.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What does the ATC term “Radar Contact” signify?

choices.text: Your aircraft has been identified and you will receive separation from all aircraft while in contact with this radar facility.
Your aircraft has been identified on the radar display and radar flight-following will be provided until radar identification is terminated.
You will be given traffic advisories until advised the service has been terminated or that radar contact has been lost.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (P/C Glossary)
radar kontakt라는 용어는 ATC에서 항공기에 레이더 디스플레이에서 식별되고 레이더 서비스가 종료될 때까지 레이더 비행이 제공된다는 것을 알리기 위해 사용됩니다.
항공기가 레이더 접촉을 할 때 의무적인 보고 포인트에 대한 보고가 필요하지 않습니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
모든 항공기에서 분리되는 것은 A, B, C급 공중공간에서만 발생합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
교통 컨설팅 서비스는 가능한 한만 제공된다.
우선순위가 높은 의무는 통제 또는 다른 제한, 교통량, 주파수 혼잡 또는 컨트롤러 작업량과 같은 우선순위가 있습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (P/C Glossary) DISCUSSION: The term “radar contact” is used by ATC to inform an aircraft that it is identified on the radar display and that radar flight following will be provided until radar service is terminated. Reporting over compulsory reporting points is not required when an aircraft is in radar contact. Answer (A) is incorrect. Separation from all aircraft occurs only in Class A, B, and C airspace. Answer (C) is incorrect. Traffic advisory service is provided only to the extent possible. Higher-priority duties take precedence, such as controlling or other limitations, volume of traffic, frequency congestion, or controller workload.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: For IFR planning purposes, what are the compulsory reporting points when using VOR/DME or VORTAC fixes to define a direct route not on established airways?

choices.text: Fixes selected to define the route.
There are no compulsory reporting points unless advised by ATC.
At the changeover points.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (AIM Para 5-3-2)
VOR/DME 또는 VORTAC 픽스를 사용하여 정해진 항로에서 아닌 직접 노선을 정의할 때, 노선을 정의하기 위해 선택된 픽스는 자동으로 비행에 대한 의무적인 보고 포인트 (라다르 접촉이 없을 때) 가됩니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
직접의 비행에서, 의무적인 보고 포인트는 픽스가 노선을 정의하는 데 사용된 점입니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
직접 비행에서 사용되는 일부 항법 시스템은 항법 가이드, 예를 들어 GPS의 손실을 방지하기 위해 COP를 필요로하지 않습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (AIM Para 5-3-2) DISCUSSION: When using VOR/DME or VORTAC fixes to define a direct route not on an established airway, those fixes selected to define the route automatically become compulsory reporting points (when not in radar contact) for the flight. Answer (B) is incorrect. On a direct flight, the compulsory reporting points are those fixes used to define the route. Answer (C) is incorrect. Some navigation systems used on direct flights do not require COPs to prevent the loss of navigation guidance, e.g., GPS.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: While performing a VFR practice instrument approach, Radar Approach Control assigns an altitude or heading that will cause you to enter the clouds. What action should you take?

choices.text: Continue as directed.
Advise “unable” and remain clear of clouds.
Deviate as needed; then rejoin the approach.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (AIM Para 4-3-21)
VFR 연습 도구 접근 동안, 당신은 기본적인 VFR 날씨 최소 사항을 준수할 책임이 있습니다.
따라서, Radar 접근 Control가 클라우드에 들어가는 고도 또는 기수방향을 지정한다면, unable를 조언하고 클라우드로부터 멀리 떨어져 있어야 합니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
VFR 연습 기기 접근를 수행할 때, 기본적인 VFR 기상 최소치를 유지해야 합니다. 따라서, 지시대로 계속해서는 안 됩니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
Radar 접근 Control unable 를 통보하고 클라우드로부터 멀리 떨어져 있어야 합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (AIM Para 4-3-21) DISCUSSION: During VFR practice instrument approaches, you are responsible to comply with basic VFR weather minimums. Therefore, if Radar Approach Control assigns an altitude or heading that will cause you to enter the clouds, you should advise “unable” and remain clear of clouds. Answer (A) is incorrect. While performing VFR practice instrument approaches, you are required to maintain basic VFR weather minimums; therefore, you should not continue as directed. Answer (C) is incorrect. You should advise Radar Approach Control “unable” and remain clear of clouds.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: You have not yet been cleared for the approach, but you are being vectored to the ILS approach course. It is clear that you will pass through the localizer course unless you take action. You should

choices.text: turn outbound and complete the procedure turn.
continue as assigned and query ATC.
turn inbound and join the final approach course.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (AIM Para 5-4-3)
일반적으로, ATC는 격차 또는 다른 이유로 최종 접근 코스를 가로지르는 것이 필요할 때 알려줍니다.
만약 당신이 접근에 대한 허가를 받지 못했고 접근 코스를 넘을 것이라는 것이 분명해지면, 당신은 당신의 기수방향에 계속 가서 ATC를 질문해야 합니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
레이더 벡터링이 진행되는 동안 ATC가 승인하지 않는 한 선회 절차를 수행할 수 없습니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
최종 접근 코스에 선회 인바운드가 아닌 기수방향을 유지해야 합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (AIM Para 5-4-3) DISCUSSION: Normally, you will be informed by ATC when it is necessary to vector across the final approach course for spacing or other reasons. If you have not been cleared for the approach and it becomes evident that you will cross the approach course, you must continue on your assigned heading and question ATC. Answer (A) is incorrect. While you are being radar vectored, you are not authorized to make a procedure turn unless cleared by ATC. Answer (C) is incorrect. You must maintain your assigned heading, not turn inbound on the final approach course.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: During a flight, the controller advises “traffic 2 o'clock 5 miles southbound.” The pilot is holding 20° correction for a crosswind from the right. Where should the pilot look for the traffic?

choices.text: 40° to the right of the aircraft’s nose.
20° to the right of the aircraft's nose.
Straight ahead.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (AIM Para 4-1-14)
ATC는 항공기의 코스 (즉, 지상 트랙) 의 관점에서 교통 자문을 발행하고, 기수방향은 아닙니다.
추동정지 또는 코스 변경은 레이더 교통 정보와 동시에 이루어져야 합니다.
2시까지는 항공기의 코스의 오른쪽으로 약 60°로 이동합니다.
조종사는 이미 체공 20°의 오른바람 교정 상태이기 때문에, 그는 교통을 위해 항공기의 코의 오른쪽으로 40°만 봐야 한다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
이 방향은 항공기의 트랙의 오른쪽으로 40°로 1~2시 사이에 있습니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
직선으로 항공기의 트랙의 오른쪽으로 20° (바람 교정) 이 있고, 이는 12시에서 1시 사이에 있습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (AIM Para 4-1-14) DISCUSSION: ATC issues traffic advisories in terms of the aircraft's course (i.e., ground track), not its heading. Allowance must be made for drift correction or course change made simultaneously with the radar traffic information. Two o'clock is approximately 60° to the right of the aircraft's course. Since the pilot is already holding a 20° right-wind correction, (s)he should look only 40° to the right of the aircraft's nose for the traffic. Answer (B) is incorrect. This direction is 40° to the right of the aircraft's track, which is between 1 and 2 o'clock. Answer (C) is incorrect. Straight ahead is 20° (wind correction) to the right of the aircraft's track, which is between 12 and 1 o'clock.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What is the pilot in command’s responsibility when flying a propeller aircraft within 20 miles of the airport of intended landing and ATC requests the pilot to reduce speed to 160? (Pilot complies with speed adjustment.)

choices.text: Reduce TAS to 160 knots and maintain until advised by ATC.
Reduce IAS to 160 MPH and maintain until advised by ATC.
Reduce IAS to 160 knots and maintain that speed within 10 knots.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (AIM Para 4-4-12)
ATC는 FL 240 이하의 10kT 증가로 지시대기속도 (IAS) 에 기반한 노트 용어로 모든 속도 조절을 표현합니다.
ATC 속도를 160으로 줄이기 위한 조정 사항을 준수할 때, IAS를 160 kt로 줄이고 그 속도를 10 kt 내에서 유지해야 합니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
ATC 속도 제한은 지시대기속도 (IAS) 에 근거하고 있으며, 진대기속도 (TAS) 에 근거하지 않습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
공기의 속도는 MPH가 아닌 노트로 주어집니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (AIM Para 4-4-12) DISCUSSION: ATC will express all speed adjustments in terms of knots based on indicated airspeed (IAS) in 10-kt. increments below FL 240. When complying with an ATC speed adjustment to reduce to 160, you should reduce IAS to 160 kt. and maintain that speed within 10 kt. Answer (A) is incorrect. ATC speed restrictions are based on indicated airspeed (IAS), not true airspeed (TAS). Answer (B) is incorrect. Airspeeds are given in knots, not MPH.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: Upon intercepting the assigned radial, the controller advises you that you are on the airway and to “RESUME OWN NAVIGATION.” This phrase means that

choices.text: You are still in radar contact, but must make position reports.
Radar services are terminated and you will be responsible for position reports.
You are to assume responsibility for your own navigation.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (P/C Glossary)
계획된 비행 경로에서 항로로 벡터링된다고 가정하면 ATC가 자신의 항법를 재개할 것을 조언할 때 항로를 사용하여 항로를 따라 코스를 유지해야 합니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
레이더 접촉 시 위치 보고는 필요하지 않습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
Res항법를 재개하면 레이더 컨트롤러가 당신을 관찰하는 것이 아니라 벡터링하는 것을 멈추게 됩니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (P/C Glossary) DISCUSSION: Assuming you have been vectored to an airway on your intended route of flight, you should maintain your course along the airway by use of your navigation equipment when ATC advises you to resume your own navigation. Answer (A) is incorrect. Position reporting is not required when in radar contact. Answer (B) is incorrect. “Resume navigation” means only that the radar controller is going to stop vectoring you, not stop observing you.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: During the en route phase of an IFR flight, the pilot is advised “Radar service terminated.” What action is appropriate?

choices.text: Set transponder to code 1200.
Resume normal position reporting.
Activate the IDENT feature of the transponder to re-establish radar contact.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (AIM Para 5-3-2)
IFR 비행의 노선 단계에서, radar 서비스 종료 또는 radar 접촉 손실에 대해 알려지면, radar 접촉이 없을 때 필요에 따라 정상적인 위치 보고를 재개해야 합니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
ATC와 함께 IFR 비행 계획을 취소하고 VFR를 윙크하도록 지시될 때만 트랜스폰더를 코드 1200 (VFR) 로 설정해야 합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
ATC의 요청에 의해서만 트랜스폰더의 IDENT 기능을 활성화해야 합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (AIM Para 5-3-2) DISCUSSION: During the en route phase of an IFR flight, if you are advised of “radar service terminated” or “radar contact lost,” you should resume normal position reporting as required when not in radar contact. Answer (A) is incorrect. You should set the transponder to code 1200 (VFR) only when you cancel your IFR flight plan with ATC and you are instructed to squawk VFR. Answer (C) is incorrect. You should activate the IDENT feature of the transponder only upon the request of ATC.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What is meant when departure control instructs you to “resume own navigation” after you have been vectored to a Victor airway?

choices.text: You should maintain the airway by use of your navigation equipment.
Radar service is terminated.
You are still in radar contact, but must make position reports.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (P/C Glossary)
계획된 비행 경로에서 항로로 벡터링된다고 가정하면 ATC가 자신의 항법를 재개할 것을 조언할 때 항로를 사용하여 항로를 따라 코스를 유지해야 합니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
XResume 항법은 레이더 컨트롤러가 당신을 관찰하는 것이 아니라 벡터링하는 것을 멈추게 한다는 것을 의미합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
ATC와 레이더 접촉할 때 위치 보고가 필요하지 않습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (P/C Glossary) DISCUSSION: Assuming you have been vectored to an airway on your intended route of flight, you should maintain your course along the airway by use of your navigation equipment when ATC advises you to resume your own navigation. Answer (B) is incorrect. “Resume navigation” means that the radar controller will stop vectoring you, not stop observing you. Answer (C) is incorrect. Position reporting is not required when you are in radar contact with ATC.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What service is provided by departure control to an IFR flight when operating from an airport within the outer area of Class C airspace?

choices.text: Separation from all aircraft.
Position and altitude of all traffic within 2 miles of the IFR pilot’s line of flight and altitude.
Separation from all IFR aircraft and participating VFR aircraft.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.130)
C급 공중공간의 외부 영역에서 ATC는 모든 IFR 항공기와 참여하는 VFR 항공기에서 분리된 IFR 비행을 제공합니다.
VFR 항공기 외부 영역에 참여하는 것은 자발적인 것입니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
IFR 비행은 다른 IFR 항공기와 교통 경보 및 충돌 해결을 제공하며 C급 공중공간의 외부 영역 내에서 참가하는 VFR 항공기만 제공합니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
ATC는 항공기의 위치와 고도를 제공하며, 위치와 고도가 당신의 비행선에서 2 NM 이내에 모든 교통의 충돌할 수 있습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (14 CFR 91.130) DISCUSSION: In the outer area of Class C airspace, ATC provides an IFR flight with separation from all IFR aircraft and participating VFR aircraft. VFR aircraft participation in the outer area is voluntary. Answer (A) is incorrect. An IFR flight is provided traffic advisories and conflict resolution with other IFR aircraft and with only participating VFR aircraft within the outer area of Class C airspace. Answer (B) is incorrect. ATC provides position and altitude of aircraft that may conflict, not position and altitude of all traffic within 2 NM of your line of flight.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: While on an IFR flight plan, you should notify ATC of a variation in speed when

choices.text: ground speed changes more than 5 knots.
average TAS changes 10 knots or 5 percent.
ground speed changes 10 MPH or more.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (AIM Para 5-3-3)
조종사가 ATC에 요청받지 않고 보고해야 할 몇 가지 사항이 있습니다.
하나는 고도에서 비행하는 평균 TAS의 변화입니다. 그것은 비행 계획에 제출된 것과 10 kt. 또는 5% (이 더 큰 것이 무엇이든) 에 차이가 있을 때.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
ATC는 대지속도가 아닌 TAS가 10 kt 이상, 5 kt 이상 또는 5% 이상 변하는 경우 알릴 필요가 있습니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
ATC는 대지속도가 아닌 TAS가 10 kt, 10 MPH가 아닌 5% 이상 변하는 경우 알릴 필요가 있습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (AIM Para 5-3-3) DISCUSSION: There are a number of things a pilot needs to report to ATC without being requested. One is a change in the average TAS at cruising altitude when it varies by 10 kt. or 5% (whichever is greater) from that filed in the flight plan. Answer (A) is incorrect. ATC should be notified if TAS, not ground speed, varies more than 10 kt., not 5 kt., or 5%, whichever is greater. Answer (C) is incorrect. ATC should be notified if TAS, not ground speed, varies more than 10 kt., not 10 MPH, or 5%, whichever is greater.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: When are you required to establish communications with the tower (Class D airspace), if you cancel your IFR flight plan 10 miles from the destination?

choices.text: Immediately after canceling the flight plan.
When advised by ARTCC.
Before entering Class D airspace.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.129)
D급 공공간으로 들어가기 전에 탑과 쌍방향 전파 통신을 해야 합니다.
따라서 IFR 비행 계획을 취소할 경우, D급 공영공간에 진입하기 전에 자신의 위치와 의도를 탑에 알려야 합니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
D급 공항에서 15마일까지 탑으로 첫 번째 통화를 하는 것은 좋은 운영 관행이지만, D급 공영 공간에 진입하기 전에야 한다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
ARTCC는 관리자가 IFR 비행 계획 취소를 승인할 때 탑에 연락하라고 조언할 수 있지만, 당신은 D급 공영 공간에 진입하기 전에 탑에 연락해야 합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (14 CFR 91.129) DISCUSSION: You must establish two-way radio communication with the tower before entering Class D airspace. Thus, if you cancel your IFR flight plan, you must notify the tower of your position and intentions prior to entering Class D airspace. Answer (A) is incorrect. While it is a good operating practice to make an initial call to the tower up to 15 mi. from a Class D airport, it is required only before entering Class D airspace. Answer (B) is incorrect. While ARTCC may advise you to contact the tower when the controller accepts your IFR flight plan cancellation, you are required to contact the tower only prior to entering Class D airspace.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What does declaring “minimum fuel” to ATC imply?

choices.text: Traffic priority is needed to the destination airport.
Emergency handling is required to the nearest usable airport.
Merely an advisory that indicates an emergency situation is possible should any undue delay occur.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (AIM Para 5-5-15)
연료 공급이 목적지에 도착하면 부당한 지연을 받아들일 수 없는 상태에 도달했을 때 최소한의 연료 상태에 대해 ATC에 알려야 합니다.
이것은 비상사태가 아니라 비상사태가 발생할 수 있다는 것을 알려주는 통보일 뿐입니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
최저 연료를 선언할 때 우선 순위가 주어질 수 있습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
최소한의 연료 경고는 비상사태가 아닙니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (AIM Para 5-5-15) DISCUSSION: You should advise ATC of your minimum fuel status when your fuel supply has reached a state in which, upon reaching your destination, you cannot. accept any undue delay. Be aware that this is not an emergency situation, but merely an advisory that indicates an emergency situation is possible should any undue delay occur. Answer (A) is incorrect. Priority may be issued when declaring an emergency, not when declaring minimum fuel. Answer (B) is incorrect. Minimum fuel advisory is not an emergency situation.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: Which of the following reports should always be reported to ATC?

choices.text: Preferred runway choice to limit taxi time.
When true airspeed (TAS) varies by 10 percent or 5 knots, whichever is less.
When leaving an assigned holding fix.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (AIM Para 5-3-3)
ATC에 특정 요청 없이 체공 픽스 또는 지점을 떠날 때 보고서를 제출해야 합니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
선호하는 이륙 활주로를 신고하는 것은 필요하지 않지만 사용 중인 활주로 이외의 활주로에 대한 요청을 할 수 있습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
평균 진대기속도의 5% 또는 10 kt, 10% 또는 5 kt를 초과하는 변동에 대한 보고가 필요합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (AIM Para 5-3-3) DISCUSSION: A report should be made to ATC without a specific request when leaving any assigned holding fix or point. Answer (A) is incorrect. Reporting your preferred takeoff runway is not required, but you can make a request for a runway other than the one in use. Answer (B) is incorrect. Reporting is required for variations in average true airspeed exceeding 5% or 10 kt., not 10% or 5 kt.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: Which procedure should you follow if you experience two-way communications failure while holding at a holding fix with an EFC time? (The holding fix is not the same as the approach fix.)

choices.text: Depart the holding fix to arrive at the approach fix as close as possible to the EFC time.
Depart the holding fix at the EFC time.
Proceed immediately to the approach fix and hold until EFC.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.185)
접근 픽스와 동일하지 않은 체공 픽스에서 쌍방향 라디오 통신 장애가 발생하면, 체공 픽스를 EFC 시간에 남겨두고 접근를 완료하십시오.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
당신은 접근 픽스에 도착하지 않고 출발합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
EFC 시간까지 체공 픽스를 떠나 접근 픽스로 이동해서는 안 됩니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (14 CFR 91.185) DISCUSSION: If you experience two-way radio communication failure at a holding fix that is not the same as the approach fix, leave the holding fix at the EFC time and complete the approach. Answer (A) is incorrect. You would leave for, not arrive at, the approach fix at the EFC time. Answer (C) is incorrect. You should not leave the holding fix to go to the approach fix until the EFC time.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: You are in IMC and have two-way radio communications failure. If you do not exercise emergency authority, what procedure are you expected to follow?

choices.text: Set transponder to code 7600, continue flight on assigned route and fly at the last assigned altitude or the MEA, whichever is higher.
Set transponder to code 7700 for 1 minute, then to 7600, and fly to an area with VFR weather conditions.
Set transponder to 7700 and fly to an area where you can let down in VFR conditions.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.185, AIM Para 6-4-2)
두방향 라디오 기능을 잃으면 ATC를 알리고 트랜스폰더를 코드7600로 변경해야 합니다.
IMC에서 양방향 라디오 통신 장애가 발생하면 지정된 노선에서 비행을 계속하고 마지막 지정된 고도 또는 MEA를 유지하십시오.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
트랜스폰더는 항상 7600로 설정되어야 하며, 1분 동안 7700로 설정되어 있지 않아야 하며, 주어진 경로와 고도 (또는 MEA) 를 유지해야 합니다.
VMC가 발견되면 VFR 아래로 비행을 계속하고 가능한 한 빨리 착륙하십시오.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
송신기를 7600로 설정해야 합니다.
IMC에 있는 동안, 당신은 할당된 노선과 고도 (또는 MEA) 를 유지해야 합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (14 CFR 91.185, AIM Para 6-4-2) DISCUSSION: When you lose two-way radio capability, you should alert ATC by changing your transponder to code 7600. If you experience two-way radio communication failure while in IMC, continue your flight on the assigned route and maintain the last assigned altitude or the MEA, whichever is higher. Answer (B) is incorrect. The transponder should be set on 7600 at all times, not 7700 for 1 min., and you must maintain your assigned route and altitude (or MEA). If VMC are encountered, continue the flight under VFR and land as soon as practicable. Answer (C) is incorrect. You should set the transponder to 7600. While in IMC, you must maintain your assigned route and altitude (or MEA).
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: You enter a holding pattern (at a fix that is not the same as the approach fix) with an EFC time of 1530. At 1520 you experience complete two-way communications failure. Which procedure should you follow to execute the approach to a landing?

choices.text: Depart the holding fix to arrive at the approach fix as close as possible to the EFC time and complete the approach.
Depart the holding fix at the EFC time, and complete the approach.
Depart the holding fix at the earliest of the flight planned ETA or the EFC time, and complete the approach.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.185)
접근 픽스와 동일하지 않은 체공 픽스에서 쌍방향 라디오 통신 장애가 발생하면, 체공 픽스를 EFC 시간에 남겨두고 접근를 완료하십시오.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
당신은 접근 픽스에 도착하지 않고 출발합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
EFC 시간은 비행 계획 ETA보다 우선입니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (14 CFR 91.185) DISCUSSION: If you experience two-way radio communication failure at a holding fix that is not the same as the approach fix, leave the holding fix at the EFC time and complete the approach. Answer (A) is incorrect. You leave for, not arrive at, the approach fix at the EFC time. Answer (C) is incorrect. The EFC time takes precedence over the flight plan ETA.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What is the appropriate transponder code in response to lost communications?
questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.185, AIM Para 6-4-2)
7600 코드는 라디오 장애 또는 통신 손실의 경우 사용됩니다.
다른 비상코드는 납치용 7500이고 일반 비상용 7700입니다.
또한, 코드 7777는 군사용 차단기용으로 지정되어 있습니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
코드 7400는 무인 항공기에 연결이 끊어지고 있습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
코드 7500는 불법적인 간섭이나 납치사건에서 사용된다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (14 CFR 91.185, AIM Para 6-4-2) DISCUSSION: Code 7600 is used in the event of a radio failure or lost communications. Other emergency codes are 7500 for hijacking and 7700 for a general emergency. Additionally, code 7777 is reserved for military interceptors. Answer (A) is incorrect. Code 7400 is reserved for an unmanned aircraft experiencing a lost link. Answer (B) is incorrect. Code 7500 is used in the event of unlawful interference or hijacking.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: In the event of unlawful interference or hijacking, which transponder code should you input immediately?
questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.185, AIM Para 6-4-2)
비분별한 트랜스폰더 코드 7500는 불법적인 간섭이나 납치사건에서 사용된다.
일단 입력하면 이 코드는 모든 레이더 ATC 시설에서 특별한 비상 표시기를 실행합니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
7600 코드는 라디오 장애 또는 통신 손실의 경우 사용됩니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
코드 7777는 4096 트랜스폰더에 입력될 수 있는 가장 높은 값 코드와 군사적 인터센터 오너레이션에 예약된 단독 코드이다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (14 CFR 91.185, AIM Para 6-4-2) DISCUSSION: The nondiscrete transponder code 7500 is used in the event of unlawful interference or hijacking. Once input, this code triggers a special emergency indicator in all radar ATC facilities. Answer (B) is incorrect. Code 7600 is used in the event of a radio failure or lost communications. Answer (C) is incorrect. Code 7777 is the highest value code that may be entered on a 4096 transponder and a discrete code reserved for military intercentor onerationsc.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What altitude and route should be used if you are flying in IMC and have two-way radio communications failure?

choices.text: Continue on the route specified in your clearance, fly at an altitude that is the highest of last assigned altitude, altitude ATC has informed you to expect, or the MEA.
Fly direct to an area that has been forecast to have VFR conditions, fly at an altitude that is at least 1,000 feet above the highest obstacles along the route.
Descend to MEA and, if clear of clouds, proceed to the nearest appropriate airport. If not clear of clouds, maintain the highest of the MEA’s along the clearance route.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.185)
IMC에서 양방향 라디오 통신을 잃으면 마지막 ATC 허가에 의해 지정된 노선, ATC가 추천한 노선 또는 비행 계획에 의해 비행을 계속하십시오.
마지막 ATC 허가, MEA 또는 비행 레벨 ATC에서 할당된 고도 중 가장 높은 것을 사용하십시오.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
주어진 경로를 계속해야 합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
주어진 고도 중 가장 높은 고도 또는 MEA를 사용해야 합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (14 CFR 91.185) DISCUSSION: When you lose two-way radio communication in IMC, continue the flight by the route assigned by the last ATC clearance, by the route that ATC has advised may be expected to be assigned, or by the flight plan. Use the highest of the altitude assigned in the last ATC clearance, the MEA, or the flight level ATC may be expected to assign. Answer (B) is incorrect. You should continue the assigned route. Answer (C) is incorrect. You should use the highest of the altitude assigned, the altitude expected to be assigned, or MEA.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: Which procedure should you follow if, during an IFR flight in VFR conditions, you have two-way radio communications failure?

choices.text: Continue the flight under VFR and land as soon as practicable.
Continue the flight at assigned altitude and route, start approach at your ETA, or, if late, start approach upon arrival.
Land at the nearest airport that has VFR conditions.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.185)
VFR 조건에서 IFR 비행 중에 라디오 오류가 발생하거나 실패 후 VFR 조건이 발생하면 조종사는 VFR 아래 비행을 계속하고 가능한 한 빨리 착륙해야합니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
이 절차는 VFR가 아닌 기기 기상 조건에서만 적용됩니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
조종사는 선량한 판단력을 행사할 수 있는 특권을 가지고 있으며, 허가되지 않은 공항이나 운항된 항공기 유형에 적합하지 않은 공항에 착륙할 필요가 없으며, 조종사는 목적지로부터 불과 몇 분 떨어진 곳에 착륙할 필요가 없습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (14 CFR 91.185) DISCUSSION: If a radio failure occurs during an IFR flight in VFR conditions or if VFR conditions are encountered after the failure, the pilot should continue the flight under VFR and land as soon as practicable. Answer (B) is incorrect. This procedure applies only if you are in instrument meteorological conditions, not VFR. Answer (C) is incorrect. The pilot retains the prerogative of exercising good judgment and is not required to land at an unauthorized airport or an airport unsuitable for the type of aircraft flown, nor is the pilot required to land only minutes short of the destination.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: While flying on an IFR flight plan, you experience two-way communications radio failure while in VFR conditions. In this situation, you should continue your flight under

choices.text: VFR and land as soon as practicable.
IFR and maintain the last assigned route and altitude to your flight plan destination.
VFR and proceed to your flight plan destination.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.185)
VFR 조건에서 IFR 비행 중에 라디오 오류가 발생하거나 실패 후 VFR 조건이 발생하면 조종사는 VFR 아래 비행을 계속하고 가능한 한 빨리 착륙해야합니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
이 절차는 VFR가 아닌 기기 기상 조건에서만 적용됩니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
비행 계획 목적지까지 가는 대신 가능한 빨리 착륙해야 합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (14 CFR 91.185) DISCUSSION: If a radio failure occurs during an IFR flight in VFR conditions or if VFR conditions are encountered after the failure, the pilot should continue the flight under VFR and land as soon as practicable. Answer (B) is incorrect. This procedure applies only if you are in instrument meteorological conditions, not VFR. Answer (C) is incorrect. You should land as soon as practicable rather than proceeding to your flight plan destination.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: The transponder should be cycled to 7700 in the event of

choices.text: a hijacking.
an emergency.
lost communications.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (AIM Para 6-4-2)
비분별한 트랜스폰더 코드 7700는 긴급 상황에서는 squawk MAYDAY에 사용된다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
코드 7700는 긴급상황을 위해 예약되어 있으며, 납치 또는 불법적인 간섭은 7500로 코딩됩니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
코드 7700는 비상사태를 위해 예약되어 있으며, 라디오 장애 또는 양방향 통신 손실은 7600로 코딩됩니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (AIM Para 6-4-2) DISCUSSION: The nondiscrete transponder code 7700 is used in the event of an emergency to “squawk MAYDAY.” Although a special indicator will alarm all control positions, pilots should understand that they may not be within a radar coverage area and should therefore continue to squawk and establish radio contact as soon as possible. Answer (A) is incorrect. Code 7700 is reserved for an emergency, whereas a hijacking or unlawful interference is coded under 7500. Answer (C) is incorrect. Code 7700 is reserved for an emergency, whereas a radio failure or loss of two-way communications is coded under 7600.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What is the hijack code?
questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.185, AIM Para 6-4-2)
송신기 코드 7500는: 나는 새로운 목적지로 납치되고/ 강제되고 있다. 500 조종사가 그의 비행기가 불법적인 간섭을 받고 있다는 사전 알림 없이 ATC에서 7500 코드는 결코 할당되지 않을 것이다.
코드 7500은 모든 레이더 ATC 시설에서 특수 비상 표시를 발동합니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
7200 코드는 정상적인 운영 절차에 사용됩니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
어떠한 경우에도 민간 비행기의 조종사는 7777 코드에 따른 트랜스폰더를 운용해서는 안 됩니다.
이 코드 는 군사적 인 인상권 을 위한 것 이다
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (14 CFR 91.185, AIM Para 6-4-2) DISCUSSION: Transponder code 7500 means: “I am being hijacked/forced to a new destination.” Code 7500 will never be assigned by ATC without prior notification from the pilot that his or her airplane is being subjected to unlawful interference. Code 7500 will trigger special emergency indicators in all radar ATC facilities. Answer (A) is incorrect. Code 7200 is used for normal operating procedures. Answer (C) is incorrect. Under no circumstances should a pilot of a civil airplane operate the transponder on Code 7777. This code is reserved for military intarcantonr nncratinne
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What action should you take if your DME fails at FL 240?

choices.text: Advise ATC of the failure and land at the nearest available airport where repairs can be made.
Notify ATC that it will be necessary for you to go to a lower altitude, since your DME has failed.
Notify ATC of the failure and continue to the next airport of intended landing where repairs can be made.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.205)
필요한 DME가 FL 240 이상에서 실패하면 조종사는 ATC에 즉시 알리고, 장비의 수리 또는 교체가 가능한 예정된 착륙의 다음 공항으로 FL 240 이상으로 운항을 계속할 수 있습니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
가장 가까운 공항이 아닌 목적지로 계속 갈 수 있고, 그곳에서 수리 작업을 할 수 있습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
ATC를 통보한 후 고도로 내려갈 필요가 없습니다.
FL 240 이상으로 계속 활동할 수 있습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (14 CFR 91.205) DISCUSSION: When required DME fails at or above FL 240, the pilot should notify ATC immediately and may continue operations at and above FL 240 to the next airport of intended landing at which repairs or replacement of the equipment can be made. Answer (A) is incorrect. You can continue to your destination, not the nearest airport, and have repairs made there. Answer (B) is incorrect. You need not descend to a lower altitude after you notify ATC. You may continue to operate at or above FL 240.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What action should you take if your No. 1 VOR receiver malfunctions while operating in controlled airspace under IFR? Your aircraft is equipped with two VOR receivers. The No. 1 receiver has Omni/ Localizer/Glide Slope capability, and the No. 2 receiver has only VOR/Localizer capability.

choices.text: Report the malfunction immediately to ATC.
Continue the flight as cleared; no report is required.
Continue the approach and request a VOR approach.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.187)
통제된 공중공간에서 IFR를 적용할 때, 비행 중에 발생한 항해, 접근 또는 통신 장비의 장애가 발생하자마자 ATC에 즉시 보고해야 합니다.
각 보고서는 다음과 같이 포함되어야 합니다: 1.
항공기 식별, 2.
3. 손상된 장비
조종사의 ATC 시스템에서 IFR에 따라 운항할 수 있는 능력이 손상된 정도, 그리고 4.
ATC로부터 지원받기 위한 지원의 성격과 범위
B번 보기 오답 해설:
ATC에 보고가 필요합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
ATC는 ILS 수신기가 작동하지 않는 경우 VOR 접근가 필요하다는 것을 알 것입니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (14 CFR 91.187) DISCUSSION: When operating under IFR in controlled airspace, you must immediately report to ATC as soon as practical any malfunctions of navigational, approach, or communication equipment occurring in flight. Each report should include the following: 1. Aircraft identification, 2. Equipment affected, 3. Degree to which the capability of the pilot to operate under IFR in the ATC system is impaired, and 4. Nature and extent of assistance desired from ATC. Answer (B) is incorrect. A report to ATC is required. Answer (C) is incorrect. ATC will know that you need a VOR approach if you report the ILS receiver inoperative.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What is the procedure when the DME malfunctions at or above 24,000 feet MSL?

choices.text: Notify ATC immediately and request an altitude below 24,000 feet.
Continue to your destination in VFR conditions and report the malfunction.
After immediately notifying ATC, you may continue to the next airport of intended landing where repairs can be made.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.205)
필요한 DME가 FL 240 이상에서 실패하면 조종사는 ATC에 즉시 알리고, 장비의 수리 또는 교체가 가능한 예정된 착륙의 다음 공항으로 FL 240 이상으로 운항을 계속할 수 있습니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
낮은 고도로 내려갈 필요가 없습니다.
목적지로 계속 갈 수 있고, 그 곳에서 수리를 할 수 있습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
IFR를 적용하더라도 정상적으로 비행을 계속하고 목적지에 수리할 수 있습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (14 CFR 91.205) DISCUSSION: When required DME fails at or above FL 240, the pilot should notify ATC immediately and may continue operations at and above FL 240 to the next airport of intended landing at which repairs or replacement of the equipment can be made. Answer (A) is incorrect. There is no need to descend to a lower altitude. You may continue to your destination and have repairs made there. Answer (B) is incorrect. You may continue your flight as normal, even under IFR, and make repairs at your destination.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: Which types of airspace are depicted on the En Route Low Altitude Chart?

choices.text: Limits of controlled airspace, military training routes, and special use airspace.
Class A, special use airspace, Class D, and Class E.
Special use airspace, Class E, Class D, Class A, Class B, and Class C.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (ACUG)
로트 저-고도 통제된 공중공간, 군사 훈련 경로 및 특수용 공중공간의 한계를 나타냅니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
A급 항공공간은 FL 180 이상의 항공공간이다.
그것은 En Route Low-고도 차트에 표시되지 않습니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
A급 항공공간은 En Route Low-고도 차트에 표시되지 않습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (ACUG) DISCUSSION: En Route Low-Altitude Charts limits of controlled airspace, military training routes, and special use airspace. Answer (B) is incorrect. Class A airspace is airspace above FL 180. It is not depicted on En Route Low-Altitude Charts. Answer (C) is incorrect. Class A airspace is not depicted on En Route Low-Altitude Charts.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: The vertical extent of the Class A airspace extends from

choices.text: 18,000 feet to and including FL 450.
18,000 feet to and including FL 600.
12,500 feet to and including FL 600.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (AIM Para 3-2-2)
A급 항공공간은 18,000피트에서 확장됩니다.
FL 600까지의 MSL
A번 보기 오답 해설:
FL 450은 제트 노선 최상위입니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
A급 공중공간의 기지는 18,000피트입니다.
MSL, 12,500피트가 아닙니다.
MSL.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (AIM Para 3-2-2) DISCUSSION: Class A airspace extends from 18,000 ft. MSL to and including FL 600. Answer (A) is incorrect. FL 450 is the top of the jet routes. Answer (C) is incorrect. The base of Class A airspace is 18,000 ft. MSL, not 12,500 ft. MSL.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: Which airspace is defined as a transition area when designated in conjunction with an airport which has a prescribed IAP?

choices.text: The Class E airspace extending upward from 700 feet or more above the surface and terminating at the base of the overlying controlled airspace.
That Class D airspace extending from the surface and terminating at the base of the continental control area.
The Class C airspace extending from the surface to 700 or 1,200 feet AGL, where designated.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (AIM Para 3-2-6)
과도기 구역은 계기접근 절차 (IAP) 를 규정한 공항과 함께 지정될 때 표면 위로 700 ft 이상으로 늘어나는 E급 공중공간이다.
E급 항공공간은 18,000 ft까지 확장되지만 포함되지 않습니다.
MSL, 즉, A급 공중공간의 기지
B번 보기 오답 해설:
과도기 영역은 D급이 아닌 E급으로 분류됩니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
과도기 지역은 E급이고 C급이 아닙니다. 항공공간이며 700 ft 이상으로 위로 확장됩니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (AIM Para 3-2-6) DISCUSSION: Transition areas are Class E airspace that extends upward from 700 ft. or more above the surface when designated in conjunction with an airport for which an instrument approach procedure (IAP) has been prescribed. Class E airspace extends up to but does not include 18,000 ft. MSL, i.e., the base of Class A airspace. Answer (B) is incorrect. A transition area is classified as Class E, not Class D, airspace. Answer (C) is incorrect. Transition areas are Class E, not Class C, airspace and extend upward from, not to, 700 ft.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: Class G airspace is that airspace where

choices.text: ATC does not control air traffic.
ATC controls only IFR flights.
the minimum visibility for VFR flight is 3 miles.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (AIM Para 3-3-1)
G급 공중공간은 A, B, C, D, E급으로 지정되지 않은 공중공간의 부분이다.
G급 항공공간에서 ATC는 어떤 기상 조건에서도 항공 교통을 통제할 권한이나 책임을 지지 않습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
ATC는 G급 공중공간에서 IFR 비행을 제어하지 않습니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
VFR 비행에 대한 최소한의 시정은 G급 공중공간에서 10,000 ft 이하의 낮 동안 3 SM가 아니라 1 SM입니다.
MSL.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (AIM Para 3-3-1) DISCUSSION: Class G airspace is that portion of the airspace that has not been designated as Class A, B, C, D, or E. In Class G airspace, ATC has neither the authority nor the responsibility for exercising control over air traffic in any weather condition. Answer (B) is incorrect. ATC does not control IFR flight in Class G airspace. Answer (C) is incorrect. The minimum visibility for VFR flight is 1 SM, not 3 SM, in Class G airspace during the day when below 10,000 ft. MSL.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What are the vertical limits of a transition area that is designated in conjunction with an airport having a prescribed IAP?

choices.text: Surface to 700 feet AGL.
1,200 feet AGL to the base of the overlying controlled airspace.
700 feet AGL or more to the base of the overlying controlled airspace.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (AIM Para 3-2-6)
과도기 구역은 계기접근 절차가 정해진 공항과 함께 지정될 때 표면 위로 700 ft 이상으로 확장되는 통제된 공중공간입니다.
과도기 구역은 위쪽에 있는 통제된 공중공간 (즉, A급 공중공간) 의 기지에서 끝난다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
전환 영역은 700피트에서 시작됩니다.
AGL, 표면이 아니라, IAP와 함께 지정되면
B번 보기 오답 해설:
과도기 지역은 1,200피트에서 시작됩니다.
AGL는 항로 노선 구조 또는 세그먼트와 함께 지정되면 계기접근를 가진 공항이 아닌
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (AIM Para 3-2-6) DISCUSSION: Transition areas are controlled airspace extending upward from 700 ft. or more above the surface when designated in conjunction with an airport for which an instrument approach procedure has been prescribed. Transition areas terminate at the base of overlying controlled airspace (i.e., Class A airspace). Answer (A) is incorrect. A transition area begins at 700 ft. AGL, not the surface, when it is designated in conjunction with an IAP. Answer (B) is incorrect. Transition areas begin at 1,200 ft. AGL when designated in conjunction with an airway route structure or segment, not with an airport with an instrument approach.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: In addition to a VOR receiver and two-way communications capability, which additional equipment is required for IFR operation in Class B airspace?

choices.text: DME, an operable coded transponder having Mode C capability, and ADS-B Out equipment.
Standby communications receiver, DME, and coded transponder.
An operable coded transponder having Mode C capability and ADS-B Out equipment.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.131)
ATC가 다른 방법으로 허가하지 않는 한, 어떤 사람이도 B급 공중공간 내에서 항공기를 운행할 수 없습니다. 그 항공기는 1.
작동 가능한 양방향 라디오, 2.
동작 가능한 4096 코드 트랜스폰더, 모드 C 기능, 3.
ADS-B Out 장비는 1090 MHz의 주파수에서 작동하거나 978 MHz의 주파수에서 UAT를 사용하여 작동하며, 4.
IFR 운용을 위해 작동 가능한 VOR 또는 TACAN 수신기
A번 보기 오답 해설:
DME가 필요하지 않습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
대기 라디오 수신기와 DME가 필요하지 않으며 트랜스폰더는 C 모드 기능을 갖춰야 한다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (14 CFR 91.131) DISCUSSION: Unless otherwise authorized by ATC, no person may operate an aircraft within Class B airspace unless that aircraft is equipped with 1. An operable two-way radio, 2. An operable 4096-code transponder having Mode C capability, 3. ADS-B Out equipment that either operates on the frequency of 1090 MHz or operates using a UAT on the frequency of 978 MHz, and 4. For IFR operations, an operable VOR or TACAN receiver. Answer (A) is incorrect. DME is not required. Answer (B) is incorrect. A standby radio receiver and DME are not required, and the transponder must have Mode C capability.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: Which of the following is required equipment for operating an aircraft within Class B airspace?

choices.text: A 4096 code transponder with automatic pressure altitude reporting equipment.
A VOR receiver with DME.
A 4096 code transponder.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.131)
ATC가 다른 방법으로 허가하지 않는 한, 어떤 사람이도 B급 공중공간 내에서 항공기를 운행할 수 없습니다. 그 항공기는 1.
작동 가능한 양방향 라디오, 2.
동작 가능한 4096 코드 트랜스폰더, 모드 C 기능, 3.
ADS-B Out 장비는 1090 MHz의 주파수에서 작동하거나 978 MHz의 주파수에서 UAT를 사용하여 작동하며, 4.
IFR 운용을 위해 작동 가능한 VOR 또는 TACAN 수신기
B번 보기 오답 해설:
DME가 필요하지 않으며, VOR 수신기는 IFR를 작동하는 경우에만 필요합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
4096 코드 트랜스폰더는 또한 모드 C 기능이 있어야 합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (14 CFR 91.131) DISCUSSION: Unless otherwise authorized by ATC, no person may operate an aircraft within Class B airspace unless that aircraft is equipped with 1. An operable two-way radio, 2. An operable 4096-code transponder having Mode C capability, 3. ADS-B Out equipment that either operates on the frequency of 1090 MHz or operates using a UAT on the frequency of 978 MHz, and 4. For IFR operations, an operable VOR or TACAN receiver. Answer (B) is incorrect. DME is not required, and a VOR receiver is only required when operating IFR. Answer (C) is incorrect. The 4096-code transponder must also have Mode C capability.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: MOAs are established to

choices.text: prohibit all civil aircraft because of hazardous or secret activities.
separate certain military activities from IFR traffic.
restrict civil aircraft during periods of high- density training activities.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (AIM Para 3-4-5)
MOA는 특정 군사 훈련 활동과 IFR 교통을 분리하기 위해 정해진 수직 및 측면 한계를 가진 항공 공간으로 구성됩니다.
MOA가 사용되고 있을 때, ATC가 IFR 분리 기능을 제공할 수 있다면, 참여하지 않는 IFR 교통이 통과할 수 있습니다.
그렇지 않으면 ATC는 참여하지 않는 IFR 트래픽을 다시 라이트하거나 제한합니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
MOA가 아닌 금지된 지역은 국가 안보를 이유로 모든 항공기를 금지합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
특정 기간 동안 항공기를 제한하기 위해 MOA가 아닌 제한된 영역을 사용합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (AIM Para 3-4-5) DISCUSSION: MOAs consist of airspace of defined vertical and lateral limits established for the purpose of separating certain military training activities from IFR traffic. When an MOA is in use, nonparticipating IFR traffic may be cleared to fly through if ATC can provide IFR separation. Otherwise, ATC will reroute or restrict nonparticipating IFR traffic. Answer (A) is incorrect. A prohibited area, not an MOA, prohibits all aircraft for reasons of national security. Answer (C) is incorrect. A restricted area, not an MOA, is used to restrict aircraft during certain periods.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What minimum aircraft equipment is required for operation within Class C airspace?

choices.text: Two-way communications, a Mode C transponder, and ADS-B Out equipment.
Two-way communications.
Transponder, ADS-B Out equipment, and DME.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (AIM Para 3-2-4)
C급 공중공간에서, 장비 요구 사항은 1090 MHz의 주파수에서 작동하거나 978 MHz의 주파수에서 UAT를 사용하여 작동하는 작동하는 쌍방향 통신 라디오, 모드 C 트랜스폰더 및 ADS-B 아웃 장비입니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
또한 C 모드 트랜스폰더와 ADS-B Out 장비가 필요합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
또한 양방향 통신 및 모드 C 기능이 요구되며, DME는 요구되지 않습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (AIM Para 3-2-4) DISCUSSION: In Class C airspace, the equipment requirement is an operating two-way communications radio, a Mode C transponder, and ADS-B Out equipment that either operates on the frequency of 1090 MHz or operates using a UAT on the frequency of 978 MHz. Answer (B) is incorrect. A Mode C transponder and ADS-B Out equipment are also required. Answer (C) is incorrect. Two-way communications and Mode C capability are also required, and DME is not required.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: Your transponder is inoperative. What are the requirements for flying in Class D airspace?

choices.text: The entry into Class D is prohibited.
Continue the flight as planned.
Pilot must immediately request priority handling to proceed to destination.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.129)
항공기의 트랜스포더가 D급 공중공간에서 비행 중 실패하면, D급 공중공간에서 트랜스포더가 필요하지 않기 때문에 경각심이 필요하지 않습니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
D급 공중공간에서 트랜스폰더가 필요하지 않기 때문에 조종사는 D급 공중공간을 떠나지 않아도 된다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
D급 공중공간에서 트랜스폰더가 필요하지 않기 때문에 조종사는 목적지까지 이동하기 위해 우선적으로 처리할 필요가 없습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (14 CFR 91.129) DISCUSSION: If an aircraft's transponder fails during flight within Class D airspace, no deviation is required because a transponder is not required in Class D airspace. Answer (A) is incorrect. Since a transponder is not required in Class D airspace, the pilot does not need to depart the Class D airspace. Answer (C) is incorrect. Since a transponder is not required in Class D airspace, a pilot does not need priority handling to proceed to his or her destination.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.question: When is an IFR clearance required during VFR weather conditions?

choices.text: When operating in the Class E airspace.
When operating in a Class A airspace.
When operating in airspace above 14,500 feet.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.135, 91.173)
어떤 사람이나 A급 공중공간에서 항공기를 운항할 수 없습니다. 항공기는 날씨 조건과 상관없이 IFR 허가에 의해 운항되지 않는 한 말이죠.
A급 항공공간은 18,000피트 MSL에서 FL 600까지의 항공공간을 포함한다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
IFR 허가는 E급 공중공간에서 VMC에서 요구되지 않습니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
IFR 허가는 E급 공중공간에서 14500피트 MSL에서 18,000피트 MSL까지 필요한 것이 아닙니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (14 CFR 91.135, 91.173) DISCUSSION: No person may operate an aircraft within Class A airspace unless the aircraft is operated under an IFR clearance, regardless of the weather conditions. Class A airspace includes the airspace from 18,000 feet MSL up to and including FL 600. Answer (A) is incorrect. An IFR clearance is not required in VMC in Class E airspace. Answer (C) is incorrect. An IFR clearance is not required in VMC in Class E airspace from 14,500 feet MSL up to but not including 18,000 feet MSL.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: When is an IFR flight plan required?

choices.text: When less than VFR conditions exist in either Class E or Class G airspace and in Class A airspace.
Inall Class E airspace when conditions are below VFR, in Class A airspace, and in defense zone airspace.
In Class E airspace when IMC exists or in Class A airspace.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.135, 91.173)
IMC의 E급 공중공간에서 항공기를 운항할 수 있는 사람은 누구든지 IFR 비행 계획을 제출하고 적절한 ATC 허가를 받은 경우를 제외하고는 없습니다.
또한, 14 CFR 91.135에 따르면, ATC가 부여한 특정 비행 수준에서 IFR에 따라 항공기가 운항하지 않는 한 A 클래스 공중공간에 아무도 운항할 수 없습니다.
이것은 또한 A급 공중공간에 대한 IFR 비행 계획을 제출했다는 것을 의미한다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
계기비행증명가 필요하지만, IFR 비행 계획은 G급 공중공간에서 필요하지 않습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
VFR 비행은 항공 방어 식별 구역 (ADIZ) 에서 VFR 기상 조건이 존재할 때 허용됩니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (14 CFR 91.135, 91.173) DISCUSSION: No person may operate an aircraft in Class E airspace in IMC unless (s)he has filed an IFR flight plan and received an appropriate ATC clearance. Furthermore, under 14 CFR 91.135, no one may operate in Class A airspace unless the aircraft is operated under IFR at a specific flight level assigned by ATC. This implies having filed an IFR flight plan for Class A airspace also. Answer (A) is incorrect. While an instrument rating is required, an IFR flight plan is not required in Class G airspace. Answer (B) is incorrect. VFR flights are permitted when VFR weather conditions exist in air defense identification zones (ADIZ).
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.question: Operation in which airspace requires filing an IFR flight plan?

choices.text: Any airspace when the visibility is less than 1 mile.
Class E airspace with IMC and Class A airspace.
Positive control area, Continental Control Area, and all other airspace, if the visibility is less than 1 mile.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.135, 91.173)
IMC의 E급 공중공간에서 항공기를 운항할 수 있는 사람은 누구든지 IFR 비행 계획을 제출하고 적절한 ATC 허가를 받은 경우를 제외하고는 없습니다.
또한, 14 CFR 91.135에 따르면, ATC가 부여한 특정 비행 수준에서 IFR에 따라 항공기가 운항하지 않는 한 A 클래스 공중공간에 아무도 운항할 수 없습니다.
이것은 또한 A급 공중공간에 대한 IFR 비행 계획을 제출했다는 것을 의미한다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
IFR 비행 계획은 G급 공중공간에서 필요하지 않습니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
통제되지 않은 G급 공중공간에서 IFR 비행 계획이 필요하지 않습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (14 CFR 91.135, 91.173) DISCUSSION: No person may operate an aircraft in Class E airspace in IMC unless (s)he has filed an IFR flight plan and received an appropriate ATC clearance. Furthermore, under 14 CFR 91.135, no one may operate in Class A airspace unless the aircraft is operated under IFR at a specific flight level assigned by ATC. This implies having filed an IFR flight plan for Class A airspace also. Answer (A) is incorrect. An IFR flight plan is not required in Class G airspace. Answer (C) is incorrect. An IFR flight plan is not required in uncontrolled Class G airspace.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.question: What is the required flight visibility and distance from clouds if you are operating in Class E airspace at 9,500 feet MSL with a VFR-on-Top clearance during daylight hours?

choices.text: 3M, 1,000 feet above, 500 feet below, and 2,000 feet horizontal.
5 SM, 500 feet above, 1,000 feet below, and 2,000 feet horizontal.
3SM, 500 feet above, 1,000 feet below, and 2,000 feet horizontal.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.155)
E급 공중공간에서 10,000 피트 MSL 이하의 기본 VFR 기상 최소는 3 SM의 비행 시정이며 구름으로부터 500 피트 아래, 1,000 피트 위, 2,000 피트 수평의 거리가 있습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
시정 요건은 SM가 아닌 3, 그리고 위의 구름과 아래 구름의 거리는 뒤집어진다.
1,000피트 높고 500피트 아래로 있어야 합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
위의 구름과 아래 구름의 거리는 뒤집어집니다.
1,000피트 높고 500피트 아래로 있어야 합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (14 CFR 91.155) DISCUSSION: In Class E airspace below 10,000 feet MSL, the basic VFR weather minimums are flight visibility of 3 SM and a distance from clouds of 500 feet below, 1,000 feet above, and 2,000 feet horizontal. Answer (B) is incorrect. The visibility requirement is 3, not 5, SM, and the distances from clouds above and below are reversed. It should be 1,000 feet above and 500 feet below. Answer (C) is incorrect. The distances from clouds above and below are reversed. It should be 1,000 feet above and 500 feet below.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What is the minimum flight visibility and distance from clouds for flight at 10,500 feet with a VFR-on-Top clearance during daylight hours? (Class E airspace.)

choices.text: 3 SM, 1,000 feet above, 500 feet below, and 2,000 feet horizontal.
5SM, 1,000 feet above, 1,000 feet below, and 1 mile horizontal.
5 SM, 1,000 feet above, 500 feet below, and 1 mile horizontal.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.155)
1만 피트 MSL 이상의 클래스 E 공중공간에서, 기본 VFR 기상 최소는 5 SM의 비행 시정 및 1,000 피트 이상의 구름과 아래의 거리와 1 SM의 수평이다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
최소한의 비행 시정 및 E 클래스 공중 공간에서 구름으로부터의 거리는 아래, 또는 위, 10,000 피트 MSL는 3 SM, 1,000 피트 위, 500 피트 아래, 2,000 피트 수평입니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
구름과 수직적으로 떨어져 있는 곳은 1,000피트 높고 아래로 있습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (14 CFR 91.155) DISCUSSION: In Class E airspace at or above 10,000 feet MSL, the basic VFR weather minimums are flight visibility of 5 SM and a distance from clouds of 1,000 feet above or below and 1 SM horizontal. Answer (A) is incorrect. The minimum flight visibility and distance from clouds in Class E airspace below, not at or above, 10,000 feet MSL are 3 SM, 1,000 feet above, 500 feet below, and 2,000 feet horizontal. Answer (C) is incorrect. The vertical separation from clouds is 1,000 feet both above and below.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.question: A flight is to be conducted in VFR-on- Top conditions at 12,500 feet MSL (above 1,200 feet AGL). What is the in-flight visibility and distance from clouds required for operation in Class E airspace during daylight hours?

choices.text: 5 miles; above 1,000 feet; horizontal 2,000 feet; below 500 feet.
5 miles; above 1,000 feet; horizontal 1 mile; below 1,000 feet.
3 miles; above 1,000 feet; horizontal 2,000 feet; below 1,000 feet.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.155)
1만 피트 MSL 이상의 클래스 E 공중공간에서, 기본 VFR 기상 최소는 비행 중인 시정 5 정규 마일 및 1,000 피트 이상의 구름과 아래의 거리와 1 정규 마일 수평이다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
클라우드로부터의 거리는 아래와 같지만, MSL 10,000피트 이상입니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
시정 요건은 3마일보다는 5마일이고, 구름으로부터 수평적인 분리 요건은 2,000피트보다는 1마일입니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (14 CFR 91.155) DISCUSSION: In Class E airspace at or above 10,000 feet MSL, the basic VFR weather minimums are in-flight visibility of 5 statute miles and a distance from clouds of 1,000 feet above or below and 1 statute mile horizontal. Answer (A) is incorrect. The distance-from-clouds requirements listed are for below, not at or above, 10,000 feet MSL. Answer (C) is incorrect. The visibility requirement is 5 statute miles, not 3 statute miles, and the horizontal separation requirement from clouds is 1 statute mile, not 2,000 feet.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.question: What is the minimum in-flight visibility and distance from clouds required for an airplane operating less than 1,200 feet AGL during daylight hours in Class G airspace?

choices.text: 3 miles; above 1,000 feet; horizontally 2,000 feet; below 500 feet.
1 mile; above clear of clouds; horizontally clear of clouds; below clear of clouds.
1 mile; above 500 feet; horizontally 1,000 feet; below 500 feet.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.155)
1,200 피트 AGL 이하의 G급 공중공간에서, 낮 시간 동안 기본 VFR 기상 최소는 비행 중 1 정규 마일의 시정이며 구름이 없습니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
최소 시정과 VFR 비행에서 낮이 아닌 밤의 구름으로부터의 거리는 3 정규 마일 시정, 1,000 피트 높고, 500 피트 아래와 2,000 피트 수평입니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
이러한 요구 사항의 조합은 어떤 항공공간에서도 존재하지 않습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (14 CFR 91.155) DISCUSSION: In Class G airspace at or below 1,200 feet AGL, the basic VFR weather minimums during daylight hours are in-flight visibility of 1 statute mile and clear of clouds. Answer (A) is incorrect. The minimum visibility and distance from clouds in VFR flight at night, not in daylight, are 3 statute miles visibility, 1,000 feet above, 500 feet below, and 2,000 feet horizontal. Answer (C) is incorrect. No such combination of requirements exists in any airspace.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What is the minimum in-flight visibility and distance from clouds required in VFR conditions above clouds at 13,500 feet MSL (above 1,200 feet AGL) in Class G airspace during daylight hours?

choices.text: 5 miles; above 1,000 feet; horizontal 2,000 feet; below 500 feet.
3 miles; above 1,000 feet; horizontal 1 mile; below 1,000 feet.
5 miles; above 1,000 feet; horizontal 1 mile; below 1,000 feet.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.155)
1,200 피트 이상의 AGL 및 10,000 피트 이상의 MSL에서 G 클래스 공중공간에서, 기본 VFR 기상 최소는 비행 중 시정 5 정규 마일 및 1,000 피트 이상의 구름과 아래의 거리와 1 정규 마일 수평이다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
1,000 피트 이상의 거리와 2,000 피트 수평, 500 피트 이하의 거리는 1,200 피트 이상의 AGL 및 10,000 피트 이상의 MSL 이하의 G 클래스 공중 공간에서 VFR에 대한 최소 클라우드 거리가입니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
시정 최소는 5마일, 3마일이 아닙니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (14 CFR 91.155) DISCUSSION: In Class G airspace at more than 1,200 feet AGL and at or above 10,000 feet MSL, the basic VFR weather minimums are in-flight visibility of 5 statute miles and a distance from clouds of 1,000 feet above or below and 1 statute mile horizontal. Answer (A) is incorrect. Distances of 1,000 feet above, 2,000 feet horizontal, and 500 feet below are the minimum cloud distances for VFR in Class G airspace above 1,200 feet AGL and below, not at or above, 10,000 feet MSL. Answer (B) is incorrect. The visibility minimum is 5 statute miles, not 3 statute miles.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What is the minimum in-flight visibility and distance from clouds required for a VFR-on-Top flight at 9,500 feet MSL (above 1,200 feet AGL) during daylight hours?

choices.text: 2,000 feet; above 1,000 feet; horizontal 2,000 feet; below 500 feet.
5 miles; above 1,000 feet; horizontal 2,000 feet; below 500 feet.
3 miles; above 1,000 feet; horizontal 2,000 feet; below 500 feet.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.155)
E급 공중공간에서 MSL 10,000 피트 미만에서, 기본 VFR 기상 최소는 비행 중 3 마일의 시정 및 500 피트 아래, 1,000 피트 위, 2,000 피트 수평의 구름으로부터의 거리가 있습니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
시정이 필요한 것은 2,000피트가 아닌 3마일입니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
시정은 5마일보다는 3마일입니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (14 CFR 91.155) DISCUSSION: In Class E airspace at less than 10,000 feet MSL, the basic VFR weather minimums are in-flight visibility of 3 statute miles and a distance from clouds of 500 feet below, 1,000 feet above, and 2,000 feet horizontal. Answer (A) is incorrect. The visibility required is 3 statute miles, not 2,000 feet. Answer (B) is incorrect. The visibility required is 3 statute miles, not 5 statute miles.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What in-flight visibility and distance from clouds is required for a flight at 8,500 feet MSL (above 1,200 feet AGL) in Class G airspace in VFR conditions during daylight hours?

choices.text: 1 mile; above 1,000 feet; horizontal 2,000 feet; below 500 feet.
3 miles; above 1,000 feet; horizontal 2,000 feet; below 500 feet.
5 miles; above 1,000 feet; horizontal 1 mile; below 1,000 feet.

questions.explanation:
정답: A
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.155)
1,200 피트 이상의 AGL, 하지만 10,000 피트 미만의 MSL의 G 클래스 공중 공간에서 낮 시간 동안 기본 VFR 날씨 최소는 비행 중 1 마일의 시정이며 구름으로부터 500 피트 아래, 1,000 피트 위, 2,000 피트 수평의 거리가 있습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
3마일의 비행기 시정은 낮이 아닌 밤의 비행을 위해 필요합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
비행 중인 시정은 5 마일 정규이며, 구름으로부터 1000 피트 이상의 거리와 1 마일 수평한 거리는 1,200 피트 AGL 이상의 G 클래스 공중공간의 VFR 기상 최소이며, 10,000 피트 MSL 이하 또는 그 이상입니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (A) is correct. (14 CFR 91.155) DISCUSSION: In Class G airspace at more than 1,200 feet AGL but less than 10,000 feet MSL, the basic VFR weather minimums during daylight hours are in-flight visibility of 1 statute mile and a distance from clouds of 500 feet below, 1,000 feet above, and 2,000 feet horizontal. Answer (B) is incorrect. The in-flight visibility of 3 statute miles is required for a night, not day, flight. Answer (C) is incorrect. In-flight visibility of 5 statute miles and a distance from clouds of 1,000 feet above or below and 1 statute mile horizontal are the VFR weather minimums in Class G airspace above 1,200 feet AGL and at or above, not below, 10,000 feet MSL.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.subject: IR Gleim
questions.study_unit_title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

subunit.title: Airports, Air Traffic Control, and Airspace

questions.question: What is the minimum in-flight visibility and distance from clouds required for an airplane operating less than 1,200 feet AGL under special VFR during daylight hours?

choices.text: 1 mile; above 2,000 feet; horizontal 2,000 feet; below 500 feet.
3 miles; above clear of clouds; horizontal clear of clouds; below 500 feet.
1 mile; above clear of clouds; horizontal clear of clouds; below clear of clouds.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.157)
E급 공중공간에서 비행기가 특별한 VFR 아래 운항할 때, 클라우드로부터의 거리가 요구되는 것은 클라우드에서 제외됩니다.
누구도 이륙 또는 비행기를 특별 VFR 아래 착륙할 수 없습니다.
지형 시정이 보고되지 않으면, 이륙 또는 착륙 중 비행중의 시정은 적어도 1 정규 마일여야 합니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
VFR는 구름이 없는 곳에서 작동할 수 있게 해줍니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
특별한 VFR는 구름에서 벗어나 최소 시정이 3마일보다는 1마일인
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (14 CFR 91.157) DISCUSSION: In Class E airspace when an airplane is operating under special VFR, the distance-from-clouds requirement is clear of clouds. No one may take off or land an airplane under special VFR unless ground visibility is at least 1 statute mile. If ground visibility is not reported, the in-flight visibility during takeoff or landing must be at least 1 statute mile. Answer (A) is incorrect. Special VFR permits operation just clear of clouds. Answer (B) is incorrect. Special VFR permits operation just clear of clouds and with a minimum visibility of 1 statute mile, not 3 statute miles.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.question: When are you required to have an instrument rating for flight in VMC?

choices.text: Flight through an MOA.
Flight into an ADIZ.
Flight into Class A airspace.

questions.explanation:
정답: C
원문 근거: (14 CFR 91.135)
어떤 사람이나 기기 비행을 할 자격을 부여하고 기기 비행 계획에 포함되지 않는 한 A 클래스 항공 공간 내에서 항공기를 운항할 수 없습니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
VMC에서 MOA를 통해 비행하기 위해 계기비행증명가 필요하지 않습니다.
B번 보기 오답 해설:
계기비행증명는 VMC의 ADIZ (공방지방 식별 구역) 에 비행할 필요가 없습니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (C) is correct. (14 CFR 91.135) DISCUSSION: No person may operate an aircraft within Class A airspace at any time unless (s)he is rated for instrument flight and is on an instrument flight plan. Answer (A) is incorrect. An instrument rating is not required for flight through an MOA in VMC. Answer (B) is incorrect. An instrument rating is not required for flight into an ADIZ (air defense identification zone) in VMC.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.question: (Refer to Figure 162 on page 193.) You are cleared to land on RWY 16L at Eugene Mahlon Sweet Field. As you break out of the clouds, you are lined up with the white lights down the center of the runway, which lets you know that you

choices.text: are on course and lined up correctly.
are off course.
should recheck the winds prior to landing.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (Airport Diagram Legend)
차트 보충에 있는 RWY 16R  34L의 설명은 CLCL,에 대한 항목을 나타냅니다. 이 항목은 중앙선 조명을 나타냅니다.
RWY 16L  34R에 대한 설명에는 그러한 항목이 없습니다.
RWY 16L에 대한 면허가 있기 때문에, 당신이 보는 빛은 RWY 16R의 중선 빛이라고 추론할 수 있습니다. 이것은 당신이 코스에서 벗어난 것을 나타냅니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
RWY 16L는 중앙선 조명 장치가 없습니다.
그러나 RWY 16R는 중추 라인 조명을 가지고 있습니다.
유진 말론의 차트 보충 페이지에서 CLCL라는 표지를 참조하십시오. 이 표는 RWY 16R에서만 중앙선 조명을 나타냅니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
당신은 코스에서 벗어났습니다.
RWY 16L에는 중앙선 조명이 없으며, 바람으로 인해 코스에서 벗어난다고 제안하는 충분한 정보가 없으며, 착륙 이전에 바람을 다시 확인해야합니다.
지금보다 더 중요한 것은 코스에서 벗어난 것을 인식하고 그에 따라 수정하는 것입니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (Airport Diagram Legend) DISCUSSION: The description of RWY 16R — 34L in the Chart Supplement shows an entry for “CL,” which indicates centerline lighting. The description for RWY 16L — 34R has no such entry. Because you are cleared for RWY 16L, you can deduce that the lights you see are centerline lights for RWY 16R, which indicates that you are off course. Answer (A) is incorrect. RWY 16L does not have centerline lighting. However, RWY 16R does have centerline lighting. See the note labeled “CL” in the Chart Supplement page for Eugene Mahlon, which indicates centerline lighting for only RWY 16R. Answer (C) is incorrect. You are off course. RWY 16L does not have centerline lighting, and there is insufficient information to suggest you are off course due to winds and should recheck the winds prior to landing. It is more important at this point that you recognize that you are off course and correct accordingly.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.question: (Refer to Figure 251 on page 195.) What is the slope of RWY 9?

choices.text: 0.4% down.
0.3% down.

questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (FAA-H-8083-16B Chap 1)
그림 251은 RWY 27의 방향으로 지향하는 화살표를  0.4% UP로 표시합니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
그림 251은 RWY 27의 방향으로 향하는 화살표를 0.4% UP로 표시합니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
그림 251 은 RWY 36 의 방향 을 가리키는 화살표 를 0. 0.3% 다운 로 표시 합니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (FAA-H-8083-16B Chap 1) DISCUSSION: Fig. 251 shows an arrow pointing in the direction of RWY 27 labeled “0.4% UP.” That indicates RWY 9, which is the reciprocal of RWY 27, is sloped 0.4% down. Answer (A) is incorrect. Fig. 251 shows an arrow pointing in the direction of RWY 27 labeled “0.4% UP.” Therefore, RWY 27 has an upslope grade of 0.4%. Answer (C) is incorrect. Fig. 251 shows an arrow pointing in the direction of RWY 36 labeled “0.3% DOWN.”

questions.question: (Refer to Figure 251 on page 195.) When lined up for takeoff on runway 4, the compass and heading indicator should read a heading of about
questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (Airport Diagram Legend)
활주로 4는 활주로 조선의 방향으로 향하는 화살표로 048.0°라는 표기법을 포함한다.
이것은 활주로 4의 실제 정렬이 48°임을 나타냅니다.
제공되는 옵션 중 050°는 올바른 기수방향에 가장 가깝습니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
비록 활주로 명칭 협약은 활주로 4가 040°와 조화를 이루는 것을 제안하지만 실제로 기수방향에는 상당한 여유가 있습니다.
이 경우, 활주로 4는 활주로 조렬의 방향으로 향하는 화살표로 048.0°를 읽는 표기법을 포함한다.
이것은 활주로 4의 실제 정렬이 48°임을 나타냅니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
활주로 4는 활주로 조선의 방향으로 향하는 화살표로 048.0°라는 표기법을 포함한다.
이것은 활주로 4의 실제 정렬이 55°가 아닌 48°라는 것을 나타냅니다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (Airport Diagram Legend) DISCUSSION: Runway 4 includes a notation that reads “048.0°” with an arrow pointing in the direction of the runway alignment. This indicates that the actual alignment of runway 4 is 48°. Of the options offered, 050° is the closest to the correct heading. Answer (A) is incorrect. Although runway naming convention would suggest runway 4 is aligned with 040°, there is in fact a considerable amount of leeway in the actual heading. In this case, runway 4 includes a notation that reads “048.0°” with an arrow pointing in the direction of the runway alignment. This indicates that the actual alignment of runway 4 is 48°. Answer (C) is incorrect. Runway 4 includes a notation that reads “048.0°” with an arrow pointing in the direction of the runway alignment. This indicates that the actual alignment of runway 4 is 48°, not 55°.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025

questions.question: (Refer to Figure 251 on page 195.) When lined up for takeoff on runway 18, the compass and heading indicator should display a heading of about
questions.explanation:
정답: B
원문 근거: (Airport Diagram Legend)
활주로 18는 활주로 조선의 방향을 가리키는 화살표와 함께 183.6°라는 표기법을 포함한다.
이것은 실제 기수방향을 184°로 회전시킬 수 있고, 나침반과 방향지시계에서 185° 정도로 쉽게 표시될 수 있음을 나타냅니다.
A번 보기 오답 해설:
비록 활주로 명칭 협약은 활주로18가 180°로 조화되어 있다고 주장하지만 실제로 기수방향에는 상당한 여유가 있습니다.
활주로 18는 활주로 조선의 방향을 가리키는 화살표와 함께 183.6°라는 표기법을 포함한다.
이것은 실제 기수방향을 184°로 회전시킬 수 있으며, 나침반 및 방향지시계에서 185° 정도로 쉽게 표시될 수 있음을 나타냅니다.
C번 보기 오답 해설:
이 답변 옵션은 활주로 17의 방향에 향하는 화살표가 있는 17173.6°와 같은 표기판을 가진 활주로 17의 경우 더 많을 것이다.
questions.explanation_en: Answer (B) is correct. (Airport Diagram Legend) DISCUSSION: Runway 18 includes a notation that reads “183.6°” in conjunction with an arrow pointing in the direction of the runway alignment. This indicates that the actual heading can be rounded to 184° and could easily display on the compass and heading indicator as about 185°. Answer (A) is incorrect. Although runway naming convention would suggest runway 18 is aligned with 180°, there is in fact a considerable amount of leeway in the actual heading. Runway 18 includes a notation that reads “183.6°” in conjunction with an arrow pointing in the direction of the runway alignment. This indicates the actual heading can be rounded to 184° and could easily display on the compass and heading indicator as about 185°. Answer (C) is incorrect. This answer option would be more for a runway 17 with a notation such as “173.6°” with an arrow pointing in the direction of a runway 17.
questions.source: Gleim Instrument Pilot FAA Knowledge Test Prep 2025
